learningOutcomes: Apply the methods taught in Living in the Future — 6 Attributes of the AI-Native Finance Pro.

lessons.content:
## "Build Me an Agent That..." — And It Exists

This is the most powerful attribute of the future finance professional.

### What It Looks Like

You say (or type):
> *"Build me an agent that reconciles staking rewards nightly."*

And it exists. No code. No tickets. No 6-month IT project. Just describe and deploy.

### Why This Changes Everything

In the old world, if you needed a tool or process automated, you had to:
1. Write a requirements document
2. Submit it to IT
3. Wait for prioritization
4. Wait for development
5. Test and iterate
6. Deploy

In the new world:
1. Describe what you need
2. It exists

### How to Start Building This Skill

1. **Pick a simple, repetitive task** — something you do weekly that follows a pattern
2. **Describe it out loud** — if you can explain it to a person, you can explain it to an agent
3. **Create the agent** — use Claude Projects, a custom GPT, or any agent platform
4. **Give it context** — upload your chart of accounts, templates, or reference data
5. **Let it run** — start with oversight, then gradually trust it

### The Mental Shift

You stop thinking "I need to do this task" and start thinking "I need to describe this task well enough that an agent can do it."

> **No code, no tickets — just describe and deploy. The most powerful attribute.**

📎 [Build Your First AI Agent as a Finance Professional](https://finney.finance/wiki/unofficial-guides-from-alyona-mysko-s-li-posts/build-your-first-ai-agent-as-a-finance-professional)
lessons.title: Attribute 1: Creates Agents by Voice

lessons.content:
## Extremely Personalized AI

Not generic answers — answers calibrated to *your* chart of accounts, *your* team, *your* style.

### What "Tuned" Means

| Generic AI | Tuned AI |
|-----------|---------|
| "Here's how to write a journal entry" | "Here's the JE for your Q2 rent accrual using account 6200-100, matching your standard template" |
| "Revenue recognition follows ASC 606" | "Based on your SaaS contracts with annual prepayment, here's how to recognize this month's revenue across your 3 product lines" |
| "Consider improving your close process" | "Your Step 4 (intercompany eliminations) took 3x longer than last month — here's why and how to fix it" |

### How to Build Tuned Intelligence

1. **Load your context** — chart of accounts, close calendar, team structure, SOPs
2. **Set preferences** — how you like reports formatted, which metrics matter, your communication style
3. **Build memory** — let the agent learn from corrections and feedback over time
4. **Specialize** — one agent per domain (AP agent, close agent, reporting agent)

### Why Personalization Compounds

Month 1: The agent knows your chart of accounts.
Month 3: It knows your common entries, your team's patterns, your CFO's preferences.
Month 6: It anticipates issues before you ask, suggests improvements based on trends, and drafts communications in your voice.

> **Not generic answers, but answers calibrated to your chart of accounts, your team, your style.**
lessons.title: Attribute 2: Intelligence Tuned to Them

lessons.content:
## Freed from Repetition, Your Output Becomes Creativity and Judgment

When AI handles the repetitive work, what's left? The stuff only humans bring to the table.

### The Shift

| Before AI | After AI |
|----------|---------|
| 70% execution, 30% thinking | 30% oversight, 70% thinking |
| "I spent 4 hours on variance commentary" | "I spent 20 minutes reviewing AI's draft and adding strategic context the board actually needs" |
| "I can't innovate — I'm buried in close" | "Close runs itself — I'm redesigning our FP&A process" |

### What "Constantly Creative" Looks Like in Finance

- **Redesigning processes** instead of just executing them
- **Asking better questions** of the data instead of just formatting it
- **Building new tools** to solve problems no one has addressed
- **Connecting dots** across departments that no one else sees
- **Challenging assumptions** because you finally have time to think

### The Creativity Flywheel

1. AI handles the task → you get time back
2. You use the time to think → you spot an improvement
3. You describe the improvement → AI builds it
4. The improvement saves more time → repeat

### This Is the Human Edge

AI can execute. AI can analyze. AI can build.

But AI can't decide what matters. Can't read the room in a board meeting. Can't know that the CFO cares about cash flow more than EBITDA this quarter. Can't build relationships with auditors.

> **Freed from repetitive work, the knowledge worker's primary output is creativity and judgment. The stuff only humans bring to the table.**
lessons.title: Attribute 3: Constantly Creative

activities.title: Attribute 4: Builds Automations on the Fly

lessons.content:
## Like Google Sheets Today — Instant, Disposable, Natural

Think about how you use spreadsheets. You don't file a ticket to create one. You don't plan it for weeks. You just... open a sheet and start working.

That's what automations become.

### The New Normal

**Need a thing? Build it in 5 minutes. Throw it away when done.**

Examples:
- Need to reformat 500 vendor names for an import? Build a quick script. Run it. Done.
- Need to check if any invoices have duplicate amounts? Build a matcher. Run it. Delete it.
- Need to visualize cash burn by week for a quick meeting? Build a chart. Present it. Move on.

### Why "Disposable" Is Powerful

Not every automation needs to be permanent. Some are single-use:

| Permanent Automations | Disposable Automations |
|----------------------|----------------------|
| Month-end close workflow | One-time data migration cleanup |
| Recurring reconciliation | Ad-hoc analysis for a board question |
| Weekly cash report | Quick format conversion for an import |
| AP invoice processing | One-time vendor dedup |

The ability to build disposable automations means you never do tedious manual work again — even for one-off tasks.

### How to Build This Muscle

Start small. Every time you catch yourself doing something manually that feels repetitive, pause and ask:
> *"Could I describe this to AI and have it build a quick tool in 5 minutes?"*

The answer is almost always yes.

> **Automations become instant, disposable, natural — like spreadsheets are today.**
lessons.title: Attribute 4: Builds Automations on the Fly

lessons.content:
## The Easiest Attribute to Start With

At least a part of every task flows through AI. Not some tasks. Not the big ones. Every task.

### What This Looks Like

| Task | How AI Touches It |
|------|------------------|
| Writing an email | AI drafts, you edit |
| Reviewing a contract | AI extracts key terms, you validate |
| Preparing a JE | AI suggests the entry, you approve |
| Running a rec | AI matches, you review exceptions |
| Building a report | AI formats the data, you add narrative |
| Planning a meeting | AI drafts the agenda from your notes |
| Responding to an audit query | AI pulls the supporting docs and drafts the response |

### The 100% Rule

The goal isn't "use AI for 50% of tasks." The goal is **AI touches 100% of tasks, even if only for 10% of the work on each one.**

Even if AI just:
- Formats your data before you analyze it
- Drafts the first sentence of your email
- Checks your math on a quick calculation
- Summarizes a document before you read it

That's AI in every task.

### How to Build This Habit

**Week 1:** Before starting any task, ask yourself: *"How can AI help with even a small part of this?"*

**Week 2:** Keep a tally. How many tasks did AI touch today? Try to hit 100%.

**Week 3:** It's automatic. You don't think about it anymore — AI is just part of how you work.

> **The easiest attribute to start with — just make sure AI touches every workflow.**
lessons.title: Attribute 5: AI in Every Task

lessons.content:
## Agent OS: The Endgame

This is where it all comes together. Not one agent doing one task — an organization of agents running coordinated workflows.

### What Orchestrated Processes Look Like

**Centralized data** — all agents read from and write to shared data stores
**Shared memory** — what one agent learns, others can access
**Coordinated workflows** — agents hand off work to each other automatically

### The Real Example: Alex Altman's 6-Agent Finance Team

Alex Altman runs a full finance function with:
- **6 specialized agents** — each owning a domain (AP, AR, reporting, reconciliation, compliance, analysis)
- **1 human** — the orchestrator who sets priorities and reviews output
- **1 accountant** — handling judgment calls and sign-offs

That's an entire finance function. Running. Today.

→ [Read the full breakdown on Substack](https://alexaltman1.substack.com/p/a-team-of-finance-agents-running)

### The Progression

| Stage | What You Have |
|-------|-------------|
| **Individual** | One agent helping you with one task |
| **Team** | 3-5 agents, each owning a workflow |
| **Function** | Agents covering most of the finance function |
| **Organization** | Agent OS — centralized data, shared memory, coordinated workflows |

### How to Think About This Today

You don't need to build an Agent OS tomorrow. But you should be thinking in this direction:

1. **Start with one agent** — pick your most painful workflow
2. **Add a second** — pick a related workflow
3. **Connect them** — let one agent's output feed another's input
4. **Build the fabric** — shared context, shared memory, shared tools

The endgame is an agent organization. But the starting point is always the same: one agent, one task, right now.

> **Agent OS: centralized data, shared memory, coordinated workflows. The endgame is an agent organization.**

- [Scaling Individual vs. Function AI Framework](https://finney.finance/wiki/capability/scaling-individual-vs-function-ai-framework)
- [Finney Lab — MCP Tools](https://finney.finance/lab)
